static_traits.name: Li Xiaoli
static_traits.family_status: Living with husband and two daughters
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with husband strained by self-guilt and self-evaluation, but husband is generally supportive; feeling embarrassed about discussing my not-good-enough with my husband
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; never received psychotherapy in the past; no similar psychological problem history
static_traits.language_features: Negative self-labels (such as 'I am a bad homeowner/housewife'), 'should' statements, frequent comparison with others, emotional reasoning; clear expression, willing to try but pessimistic about change

basic_info.main_problem: 'I often feel I am a terrible homeowner because decorations were put up late, which makes me feel guilty and self-inadequate. These feelings started a few months ago when I missed the time to put up Christmas decorations. I attribute the cause to the pressure of maintaining a perfect home environment. The problem has gradually worsened; now I also feel guilty about not being able to complete other housework. These feelings appear whenever I notice a gap between 'what I should do' and 'what I am doing'. I tried improving organizational skills and setting reminders, but the guilt remains.'
basic_info.core_demands: 'I realized these feelings of guilt are affecting my mood and my relationships with family, so I decided to seek counseling.'
growth_experiences: Missing the window to put up Christmas decorations on time a few months ago was the start of the problem; because Christmas has always been an important tradition in her family, she viewed the untimely decorating as 'ruining the holiday', triggering significant guilt and Self-denial, which spread to other housework responsibilities.

Grew up from childhood in a family atmosphere that values Christmas ('Christmas has always been a big thing in my family'); this value condition made her strongly associate holiday decorating with self-worth as a mother/housewife, forming high expectations of a 'perfect home environment'.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough, unworthy of recognition
If I am not perfect, it equals failure

special_situations.event: Not being able to put up Christmas decorations on time a few months ago
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot complete the holiday decorating on time, I am incompetent and will 'ruin the family's holiday'
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding further mistakes by strengthening organization and time management (setting reminders, trying to be more orderly)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have let my family down; I am a terrible homeowner / housewife

special_situations.event: Not being on time or 'good enough' with daily housework (e.g. laundry, cooking, cleaning)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Housework must be completed on time and perfectly, otherwise I am a failure in all aspects
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Raising self-demands, constantly criticizing myself to force myself to meet standards

special_situations.event: Notices the gap between 'what I should do' and 'what I am doing'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I must always meet the high standards I set for myself, otherwise I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Uses 'should/must' self-demands, trying to reach the standard through stricter self-restraint
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should have done all of these; not doing them now means I am incompetent

special_situations.event: Sees other families' 'perfect' home presentations on social media
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my home is not as perfect as others', I am worse than them and inferior to others
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently comparing, raising standards, avoiding discussing my not-good-enough with my husband to avoid 'exposing inadequacy'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Why can I not be like them? I just cannot do it

special_situations.event: Husband says he does not mind, and the children have not noticed the late decorating either
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Even if they say they do not mind, they will still be disappointed inside
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continues self-blame, believing that through self-blame he can avoid disappointing family again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just comforting me; I really have disappointed them

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be a 'perfect' housewife / mother recognized by family, maintaining acceptance and a sense of worth
core_conflict.fear: Fearing disappointing family, being judged as incompetent, thus losing recognition and closeness
defense_goal: Maintains control and avoids failure by internalizing high standards and self-blame
Staying alert to inadequacy to prevent 'disappointing family' again

object_relations.object_representation: Family who are easily dissatisfied with me or let down by me
Perfect, flawless others and groups serving as judgment benchmarks
